extracted.intended_audience: IP practitioners, patent applicants, and corporate clients interested in Brazilian patent prosecution (clients of the law firm)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes proposed INPI (Brazilian Patent Office) goal to reduce patent grant delay to two years and discusses relevant procedural provisions of Brazil's Industrial Property Act that affect timing (Sections 32 and 33) and applicant options. Useful for applicants and advisers planning prosecution strategy in Brazil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 33 — maximum period to request examination (36 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Section 33 guarantees the applicant a maximum period of 36 months to request the examination."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication discussed: to preserve applicants' prerogative, a reasonable implementation of the INPI goal would be to measure the 2-year decision target from the request for examination (not from filing), because applicants may request examination in advance or wait up to 36 months. Note that applicants who request examination later should expect the 36-month filing-to-request allowance to remain available unless the IP Act is amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 32 — voluntary amendments limited until examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: "Section 32 sets forth that voluntary amendments to patent applications are only possible as long as the applicant files them until the moment in which the examination is requested."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a trade-off: the sooner an applicant requests examination (to obtain a faster grant), the sooner the window for voluntary amendments closes. Applicants should weigh the benefit of faster prosecution against the need for time to amend claims/specification. This concern was highlighted as a practical issue to resolve if examination timelines are shortened.

rubrics_metrics.name: INPI proposed target — grant patents within 2 years
rubrics_metrics.description: "The President of the Brazilian Patent Office (INPI) ... plans to reduce the delay for granting patents to only 2 (two) years from the filing of the patent application in Brazil."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes stakeholder support for speeding up grants but also emphasizes a likely implementation nuance: associations suggested the goal be framed as issuing a decision on the merits within 2 years from the request for examination (preserving applicants' Section 33 rights). The INPI proposal would be a considerable improvement relative to current delays, but practical/legislative issues may need to be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early examination option (can be requested at filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: "applicants may now already request the examination in advance, along with the patent filing"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation/implication: applicants who need fast grants should consider requesting examination early (including at filing) to benefit from any acceleration; however, doing so shortens the voluntary amendment window per Section 32. The news highlights early examination as very important for companies seeking rapid grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current average delay metric — ~49 months from request for examination (2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The average delay for a decision on the merits to be issued by the INPI, measured by patents granted throughout 2022, was 49 months counted as of the request for examination"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual benchmark: shows current baseline (~49 months) against which the proposed 2-year target would be a substantial improvement. Useful for applicants and policymakers evaluating feasibility and impact of the INPI target.
